label: Hachiman system
definition: A phage defense system in which an organism possesses a Hachiman locus encoding a HamA/HamB nuclease-helicase core that restricts bacteriophage propagation through DNA cleavage.
exact_synonyms: Hachiman antiphage defense system|Hachiman defense system
observations: Hachiman branch under phage defense system; distinct from individual hamA, hamB, or hamC genes, HamA/HamB proteins, HamAB nuclease-helicase activity, type I/II Hachiman locus subtypes, DUF1837/Cap4 domain families, source database rows naming one predicted Hachiman locus, DNA-damage sensing or DNA-cleavage subactivities, phage-encoded anti-Hachiman triggers, and other antiphage systems such as BREX, DISARM, CBASS, Gabija, Thoeris, Zorya, phosphorothioate defense, CRISPR-Cas, and abortive infection families.
